_doc: Every word the game shows. A page is {who, lines}; `who` names a portrait (or empty). With a portrait a line holds 36 characters, without one 46. The `fit` harness check fails on any line that spills out of its window.

lines: The Saltmarch is a chain of tidal islands,
strung around a whirlpool called the Maw.
Six bronze bells hang on its rim. Their
ringing keeps the Grey Tide asleep: a silt
that turns all it touches to salt-stone.
One grey morning the bells fell silent.
Captain Ossery Grane and his Brinecrow
raiders had cut them down, to sell the
bronze in far harbours.
The tide is rising, wardens. I can
taste it in the lamp-oil.
Bring the bells home. One on each
island, and a guardian on each bell.
I am too old and too slow for climbing.
But I keep a good lantern, and I keep
count. Come back here between islands,
and I will tell you what I know.
Mangrove Reach first. The raiders
moor there to take on water.
Mind the roots. Climb the trunks when
the way is blocked. Vell the Netter
holds the first bell.
Lantern Harbor. My old home, before
the raiders took the piers.
Their bottle-throwers keep their
distance. Close it. And the crabs
have armour in front: hit from behind.
The Stilt Village trades with anyone,
even Brinecrows. The Tallyman counts
their coin there.
Ropes run between the houses. High
paths and low paths both go through.
Gullstone Cliffs. Up, and up, and up.
Old Grey nests at the top. She is no
raider, but she guards that bell like
an egg. Watch the sky when she dives.
The Drowned Abbey. The bell-keepers
built it, long before the raiders.
The inner gate is locked. The key hangs
in the gallery, up the western column.
The last bell is on the Brinecrow
herself, Grane's flagship.
He knows you are coming. Carry tonics.
Whatever happens on that deck, the
bells must ring together.
Six bells. I never thought I would
hear them all again.
Warden! They tied me to the roots
and took my boat.
Take these knives. Use the item
button to throw them.
The piers used to be lit all night.
Now the raiders drink the lamp-oil.
Here, a tonic. Drink it when you
are hurt; it mends you whole.
The Tallyman keeps every coin he
ever took in that ledger of his.
Take this fury salt. With it, the
Tide Cleave costs you nothing.
I came up for gull eggs and could
not get down again.
Take a feather from the nest. It
makes your jumps light for a while.
I was the last bell-keeper here.
The halls flooded when the bells
stopped.
This charm calls up a squall. It
strikes all the foes you can see.
I was a sail-maker. They pressed me
into Grane's crew.
Take this heartroot. It makes your
heart stronger for good.
A warden? On my water?
I have netted eels bigger than you.
The bell stays in my boat.
* The great crab clacks its hammers
against the pier. Its shell is
plated with iron from a dozen hulls.
It charges. *
One bell, bronze, heavy. Worth
four hundred crowns on the mainland.
You would take it for nothing?
That is not how accounts work.
* Old Grey spreads her wings over
the bell in her nest. She has
seen off eagles. She screams. *
...a bell... was taken... from
this house...
...none shall take... another...
So you are the one ringing my bells.
Do you know what bronze fetches in
the south? More than your islands
will be worth when the tide comes in.
When the tide comes in, there will
be no south left to sell to.
Put down the sword, Grane.
No... NO. If I cannot have the
bells, the tide can have them.
And me with them!
Grane leaps to the rail as the
sea turns grey and thick beneath
the ship. The silt rises up his
boots, his coat, his throat...
WARDEN.
THE TIDE REMEMBERS EVERY SHORE.
IT WILL HAVE THEM ALL.
The six bells are hung on the rim of
the Maw again, one on every island.
At dawn they ring together.
The grey silt shivers, slackens, and
slides back into the deep. Salt-stone
crumbles to plain sand on the shore.
Listen to that. You can hear it
from every island at once.
Well rung, wardens. Well rung.
The Brinecrows scatter to the south.
The piers of Lantern Harbor are lit
again, all night long.
The tide is only the tide.

credits: An original game on the rules of
Design, code, art, music and words
in Genesis Plus GX and a disassembly
Sprites and tiles: the Aseprite format
Backdrops and the Silt King: Blender
The world, its people and its story

june: Two hook-knives: quick, two hits a cut.
brannoch: The bell-founder who cast the six.
A boarding anchor: slow, heavy, long.

help: MOVE          arrows or WASD / D-pad, stick
JUMP          Z, K or Space / A (Cross)
TIDE CLEAVE   V or I / Y (Triangle)
PAUSE, ITEMS  Enter or Esc / Start
Down + JUMP drops through a thin ledge.
Up on a trunk, rope or mast climbs it.
Attack three times for cut, cut, spin.

items.feather: Gull feather: light jumps for 15 s.
items.squall: Squall charm: strikes all foes in view.
items.fury: Fury salt: free Tide Cleaves for 20 s.
items.key: Abbey key: walk into the locked gate.

code_help: Write down your tide-code. Enter it on
the title screen to go on from here.
